description: Watson got married
Holmes was summoned to Odessa for the Trepoff murder case
Holmes cleared up the singular tragedy of the Atkinson brothers at Trincomalee
Holmes accomplished a delicate and successful mission for the reigning family of Holland
Watson was returning from a journey to visit a patient
Watson's path led him through Baker Street
Watson looked up and saw Holmes's figure pass twice in silhouette against the blind
Watson rang the bell at Holmes's residence
Watson was shown up to the chamber that had formerly been partly his own
Holmes waved Watson to an armchair
Holmes threw his case of cigars across to Watson
Holmes indicated a spirit case and gasogene in the corner
Holmes stood before the fire and looked Watson over
Holmes made deductions about Watson's weight gain, marriage, practice, and recent activities
Watson had a country walk on Thursday and came home in a dreadful mess
Watson's wife gave Mary Jane notice
Holmes chuckled to himself and rubbed his long, nervous hands together
Holmes explained his process of deduction about Watson's shoe marks and medical profession
Watson laughed at the ease with which Holmes explained his process of deduction
Watson remarked that Holmes's reasoning always appears ridiculously simple after explanation
Holmes lit a cigarette and threw himself down into an armchair
Holmes demonstrated the difference between seeing and observing using the example of steps
Holmes threw over a sheet of thick, pink-tinted notepaper to Watson
The pink-tinted notepaper came by the last post
Watson carefully examined the writing and paper of the mysterious note
Watson deduced that the note writer was well-to-do based on the expensive paper
Holmes had Watson hold the paper up to the light to examine the watermark
Holmes took down a Continental Gazetteer to look up the watermark reference
Holmes discovered the paper originated from Egria in Bohemia through the gazetteer
Holmes deduces that the note was written by a German based on linguistic analysis
A horse-drawn carriage arrives outside Holmes's residence
Someone pulls the bell at Holmes's residence
Holmes whistles in response to hearing the carriage
Watson suggests that he should leave before the client arrives
Holmes tells Watson to stay and sit in the armchair
Heavy footsteps are heard approaching on the stairs and in the passage
Someone knocks loudly and authoritatively on the door
Holmes calls out for the visitor to come in
A very tall man in rich, elaborate clothing enters Holmes's room
The masked visitor describes his physical appearance and clothing to Holmes and Watson
The masked visitor asks Holmes about receiving his note
Holmes offers the visitor a seat and introduces Watson
The visitor identifies himself as Count Von Kramm, a Bohemian nobleman
Watson rises to leave but Holmes catches his wrist and pushes him back into his chair
The Count shrugs his broad shoulders in response to Holmes's insistence
The Count binds Holmes and Watson to absolute secrecy for two years
Holmes and Watson promise to maintain secrecy
Holmes settles into his armchair and closes his eyes
Holmes slowly reopens his eyes and looks impatiently at his client
The visitor springs from his chair and paces the room in agitation
The visitor tore the mask from his face and hurled it upon the ground
The visitor declared himself to be the King
Holmes revealed he already knew the visitor was Wilhelm von Ormstein, King of Bohemia
The King sat down once more and passed his hand over his forehead
The King came incognito from Prague to consult Holmes
The King made the acquaintance of Irene Adler during a visit to Warsaw
Watson looked up Irene Adler's information in Holmes's index
Holmes recited Irene Adler's biographical details from memory
Holmes and the King discuss payment options to recover the photograph
Five attempts were made to steal the photograph from Irene Adler
Burglars in the King's pay twice ransacked Irene Adler's house
Irene Adler's luggage was diverted when she travelled
Irene Adler was twice waylaid in attempts to recover the photograph
Holmes laughed at the situation
Holmes described the case as a pretty little problem
The King responded reproachfully about the seriousness of the matter
The King announced he is about to be married
The King identified his bride as Clotilde Lothman von Saxe-Meningen
Irene Adler threatened to send the photograph to ruin the King
Adler declared she would send the photograph on the day the betrothal is publicly proclaimed
Holmes yawned while calculating the time remaining
The King took a chamois leather bag containing money from under his cloak and placed it on the table
Holmes scribbled a receipt on a sheet of his note-book and handed it to the King
Holmes took a note of Irene Adler's address
The King departed in his royal brougham
Watson arrived at Baker Street at three o'clock precisely
Holmes left the house shortly after eight o'clock in the morning
Watson sat down beside the fire to await Holmes's return
A drunken-looking groom entered the room, who was actually Holmes in disguise
Holmes vanished into the bedroom and emerged five minutes later in respectable tweed suit
Holmes stretched out his legs by the fire and laughed heartily for some minutes
Holmes choked and laughed until he was obliged to lie back limp and helpless in the chair
Holmes left the house disguised as a groom out of work
Holmes found Briony Lodge villa
Holmes walked around and examined the house closely from every point of view
Holmes helped the ostlers rub down their horses
Holmes received twopence, a glass of half-and-half, two fills of tobacco in exchange for his help
Holmes obtained information about Miss Adler and other neighborhood residents
Watson listened to all the cabmen had to tell about Godfrey Norton
Watson began to walk up and down near Briony Lodge and think over his plan of campaign
A hansom cab drove up to Briony Lodge and a gentleman sprang out
Godfrey Norton brushed past the maid and entered the house
Norton paced up and down in the sitting-room, talking excitedly and waving his arms
Norton emerged from the house looking even more flurried than before
Norton pulled a gold watch from his pocket and looked at it earnestly
Norton shouted urgent directions to drive to Gross & Hankey's and then to Church of St. Monica
Norton and the cabman drove away quickly
A neat little landau came up the lane with a hastily dressed coachman
The woman shot out of the hall door and into the landau
The woman cried directions to go to Church of St. Monica with urgent payment offer
Holmes decided between running or perching behind the landau when a cab appeared and he jumped in
Holmes told the cab driver to go to the Church of St. Monica with a time incentive
Holmes's cab raced to the church but arrived after the others
Holmes paid his cab driver and hurried into the church
Godfrey Norton ran to Holmes and urgently asked him to serve as witness
Holmes was dragged to the altar and served as witness for the marriage of Irene Adler to Godfrey Norton
The bride gave Holmes a sovereign as payment
The newlyweds separated at the church door, going to different destinations
Irene announced she would drive out in the park at five as usual
Holmes orders cold beef and beer from Mrs. Turner
Holmes recruits Watson for cooperation in breaking the law
Mrs. Turner brings in the food tray
Holmes explains his plan while eating
Holmes disappeared into his bedroom to prepare for his new role
Holmes returned from his bedroom disguised as a Nonconformist clergyman
Holmes and Watson departed from Baker Street at quarter past six
Holmes and Watson arrived at Serpentine Avenue ten minutes before seven
Holmes and Watson paced up and down in front of Briony Lodge waiting for its occupant
The street lamps were being lit at dusk
Two attempts were made to waylay and search Irene Adler for the photograph
Briony Lodge was burgled twice
Irene Adler's carriage arrives at Briony Lodge
Two loafers quarrel over who will open the carriage door
A fierce fight breaks out involving guardsmen, loungers, and a scissors-grinder
Irene Adler steps from her carriage and becomes center of the struggle
Holmes dashes to protect Irene but is struck and falls bleeding
The guardsmen and loungers flee when Holmes falls
Better dressed bystanders crowd in to help Irene and attend to Holmes
Irene Adler hurries up the steps but stops to look back at the scene
Irene agrees to let the crowd bring the injured Holmes into her sitting-room
Holmes was carried into Briony Lodge and laid out in the principal room
Watson took the smoke-rocket from under his ulster
Holmes sat up on the couch and motioned like a man who needs air
A maid rushed across and threw open the window
Watson tossed the rocket into the room crying 'Fire!' at Holmes's signal
The whole crowd of spectators joined in a general shriek of 'Fire!'
Holmes assured everyone from within that it was a false alarm
Watson slipped through the shouting crowd and made his way to the corner of the street
Watson found Holmes and they walked away together from the scene
Holmes explained that everyone in the street was an accomplice engaged for the evening
Holmes explained how he used red paint to fake his injury
The accomplices carried the disguised Holmes into Irene Adler's house
They laid Holmes on a couch in the sitting-room
The accomplices were compelled to open the window
The alarm of fire was executed by Watson
Irene Adler rushed to secure the photograph behind the sliding panel
Holmes caught a glimpse of the photograph as Adler half drew it out
Holmes cried out that it was a false alarm
Adler replaced the photograph in its hiding place
Adler rushed from the room after replacing the photograph
Holmes rose and escaped from the house making his excuses
Someone passing by greets Sherlock Holmes good-night on the street
Watson sleeps at Baker Street that night
The King of Bohemia rushes into the room while Holmes and Watson are having breakfast
They descend and start off once more for Briony Lodge
Irene Adler marries Godfrey Norton
Holmes, Watson, and the King arrived at Briony Lodge in Serpentine Avenue
An elderly woman at Briony Lodge greeted Sherlock Holmes by name
The elderly woman announced that Irene Adler left that morning with her husband by train to the Continent
Holmes pushed past the servant and rushed into the drawing-room, followed by the King and Watson
Holmes, Watson, and the King discovered the drawing-room furniture scattered and drawers open, showing signs of hurried ransacking
Holmes pulled out a photograph and letter from a hidden compartment behind the bell-pull
Holmes tore open the letter and all three men read it together
Irene Adler wrote a letter to Sherlock Holmes at midnight of the preceding night
Irene Adler realized she had betrayed herself after the fire alarm
Irene Adler was warned against Holmes months ago
Irene Adler was given Holmes's address
Irene Adler sent John the coachman to watch Holmes
Irene Adler ran upstairs and changed into her walking clothes
Irene Adler followed Holmes to his door
Irene Adler wished Holmes good-night
Irene Adler went to the Temple to see her husband
Irene and Godfrey Norton decided that flight was their best resource
The King of Bohemia exclaimed about what a woman Irene was after reading the letter
The King slipped an emerald snake ring from his finger and offered it to Holmes as a reward
Holmes requested Irene's photograph as his reward instead of the ring
The King agreed to give Holmes Irene's photograph
Holmes bowed and departed with Watson to his chambers, ignoring the King's outstretched hand
